evals.prompt: Evaluate the repo at https://github.com/alan-turing-institute/the-turing-way and give me a full scored evaluation with JSON and Markdown output.
evals.expected_output: A scored evaluation of the-turing-way across all 6 rubric categories with JSON manifest and Markdown report
assertions: Output includes both a JSON file and a Markdown file
JSON contains schema_version, generated_at, and evaluations array
All 6 scoring categories are present: activity_and_freshness, community_health, documentation_quality, technical_health, security_posture, ecosystem_fit
Each category has score, max, and details fields
total_score is the sum of all category scores
rating is one of: Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor, Critical
The evaluation uses gh API or acknowledges GitHub data was used
Markdown report includes a score table with all 6 categories
Strengths and concerns lists are present and non-empty
A recommendation paragraph is included
Data sources section notes what data was actually available

evals.prompt: I have several repos cloned in my upstream/ directory. Generate a manifest evaluating all of them and rank them by overall health.
evals.expected_output: A batch manifest.json and manifest.md with evaluations of all repos in upstream/, sorted by score
assertions: The skill scans the upstream/ directory to find repos
Output includes manifest.json and manifest.md
manifest.json has evaluations array with one entry per repo
manifest.md starts with a summary table sorted by score (highest first)
Each repo has all 6 scoring categories evaluated
Repos without .git directories are handled gracefully (noted as non-git or skipped with explanation)
If GitHub remotes are detected, GitHub API data is fetched
The summary table includes repo name, total score, and rating for each

evals.prompt: Compare these two repos and tell me which one I should depend on: https://github.com/yamadashy/repomix vs https://github.com/anthropics/sdk-python
evals.expected_output: A comparison evaluation of both repos with a clear recommendation on which to choose
assertions: Both repos are evaluated with the full rubric
Output includes comparison.json and comparison.md
A side-by-side comparison table is present
Each category score is shown for both repos
Relative strengths and weaknesses are identified for each
A clear recommendation is made with reasoning
The recommendation considers the user's context (dependency use case)

evals.prompt: Evaluate the local repo at . and tell me what I should improve to make it healthier.
evals.expected_output: Evaluation of the current directory as a repo, with actionable improvement suggestions
assertions: The skill runs evaluate_repo.py or equivalent git commands on the current directory
All 6 categories are scored
Low-scoring categories get specific, actionable improvement suggestions
Missing community files (README, LICENSE, etc.) are called out specifically
Suggestions are prioritized by impact (e.g., adding a LICENSE is more important than adding badges)
Output includes both JSON and Markdown
The tone is constructive, not just a list of failures
